points.quote: `common/` holds shared contracts and models that don't depend on the UI. ... `browser/` holds the shell and layout. ... `electron-browser/`, the desktop startup layer.
`api/`, the bridge to the extension host and the `vscode.d.ts` provider.
`services/` holds the core service implementations (about 660 files).
Nothing outside `contrib/` may depend on `contrib/`. The exceptions are the entry-point files, `api/` (356 imports) and tests.
Each contribution has a single `.contribution.ts` entry point, which registers it.
A contribution exposes its internal API from a single `common` file.
Other contributions may depend only on that common API and must not reach into a feature's internals.
